answer: knoll is a registry grown as a tree: an umber enters only countersigned by two branches at one depth that share no member, and a branch admits its cohort only once every branch above it is full. Registering at depth d burns zenith equal to the edges beneath that branch, doubling each level. A thousand clones cannot fan out sideways; they stack, and the thousandth pays a thousand zenith for one seat, at a depth reachable only by filling the cheaper ones first. The bill is zenith burned per umber, rising with depth. It breaks if branches are minted off-tree or cohorts overfilled.
